title: Nonlinearity management of matter-wave vector solitons of Bose-Einstein condensates in two dimensions
authors: F. Kh. Abdullaev, J. S. Yuldashev, M. Ögren
abstract: The evolution of matter-wave vector solitons in two dimensions under nonlinearity management is studied. The averaged over strong and rapid modulations in time of the inter-species interactions vector Gross-Pitaevskii equation is derived. The averaging gives the appearance of the effective nonlinear quantum pressure depending on the population of the other component. Using this system of equations, the dynamical stabilization of the two-dimensional vector matter-wave solitons under the management of the mean-field nonlinearity is investigated. It is shown that the nonlinear quantum pressure arrests the collapse in the averaged system, giving rise to stable vector solitons. Full numerical simulations of the original, time-dependent system of Gross-Pitaevskii equations confirm that the management strongly prolongs the lifetime of these solitons compared to the unmanaged case.
summary: This paper analyzes how periodically modulating inter-species interactions can stabilize matter-wave vector solitons in two-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensates. By deriving an effective, averaged equation, the authors show that the resulting nonlinear quantum pressure counteracts the collapse tendency inherent in the system. Numerical simulations confirm that this management technique substantially prolongs the soliton's lifetime.
main_problem: The study investigates the nonlinear management of matter-wave vector solitons in two dimensions, specifically addressing the mechanism by which this management prevents collapse.
main_result: The nonlinear quantum pressure arising from the averaging process arrests the collapse, leading to the existence of stable vector solitons whose lifetime is significantly prolonged compared to the unmanaged case.
method: The analysis employs averaging techniques over fast temporal modulations of the inter-species interaction, leading to an effective Hamiltonian, which is then analyzed using variational methods and numerical simulations.
model_or_system: The system models a two-component Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) governed by coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equations. The dynamics are analyzed under periodic modulation of the inter-species interaction, leading to an effective, averaged nonlinear quantum pressure term.
key_observables: Mean square radius ($ ar{X}(t)$), soliton width ($w(t)$), and the effective energy functional ($ ar{H}(L)$).
important_parameters: Modulation strength ($\sigma^2$), coupling constants ($g_{ij}$), and the finite width ($L_{\min}$) where stable solitons exist.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the modulation is strong and rapid, allowing for the derivation of an averaged system via a near-identity transformation; the rigorous proof of collapse arrest is limited to this averaged model.
figures_summary: Figures compare the time evolution of width and density profiles for managed vs. unmanaged systems, showing stable oscillations when management is active and collapse when it is switched off.
paper_structure: The paper first derives the averaged system by averaging the time-dependent GPEs. It then uses variational analysis to map the dynamics to a mechanical system with an effective potential. Finally, it compares the predictions of the averaged model with full numerical simulations to confirm the stabilization effect.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the stability of matter-wave solitons in BECs, a core topic in AMO physics. The concept of 'nonlinearity management' provides a novel, controllable mechanism to stabilize quantum states against collapse, which has implications for realizing robust quantum matter-wave devices.

Figure 4 shows the density |u|2 of the original model of Set B, initiated with the variationally found stationary state of the averaged system. In the first 4 frames the management is on; the wave packet keeps a localised core over many internal periods, breathing about the stationary width, and loses only the fraction of its norm that reaches the absorbing layer. In the last frame the same initial data are propagated with γ1 = 0, i.e. with the mean coupling γ0 alone: since N0 > Nc the packet collapses, and the run has to be terminated.
